items.title: Regarding Quiz-2 || Grades do not matter; learning does. || IMPORTANT READ
items.message: Dear All, I would like to begin with a saying that is especially relevant today: "Grades do not matter; learning does." If you felt that today's questions were difficult, you must practice the provided code at home. I have always mentioned that you need to spend at least nine hours each week on this course to excel. The questions on the quiz were not difficult; each one was straightforward. Please take this quiz as an evaluation of your knowledge in JavaScript. Since we are working within a JavaScript-everywhere paradigm, it is very important that you have a strong foundation in JavaScript. Every piece of code we have covered so far will be used in Express.js, and later with database integration and React.js. Once again, I strongly encourage you to practice the provided code at home. items.title: Get involved in the SVSU Department of Theatre Productions
items.message: Would you like to be involved in the design and crew positions for the upcoming productions for the SVSU Department of Theatre? items.title: A Note from the columbinus Director
items.message: Please read the  columbinus  script with caution . It contains many difficult topics and themes. It is a stylized telling of the events of the 1999 Columbine High School shootings. It uses elements of  "Verbatim Theatre. , where lines in the play and things discussed are directly quoted from the people who said them or witness/police statements/records. This makes some of the reading difficult and challenging. The language and vocabulary in the play is also challenging. As with any "Verbatim Theatre", quotes are included as they were said and not edited or censored.  You ca

items.message: The Miser: Performed in the style of Commedia Dell’Arte, this classic comedy of money versus love revolves around the central character, Harpagon, a wealthy but miserly old man who values his money above all else. items.title: Wednesday Weather Advisory
items.message: Hi Everyone, I have my eye on the weather radar for tomorrow's expected storm. After talking to the department head, we are going to follow university protocol; if the university cancels classes, we will cancel classes and rehearsal. If classes are not cancelled, I will be in rehearsal and there will be no online option since it is a hands-on workshop instead of a lecture.   Please have your SVSU alerts set and keep your eye on Canvas announcements for any updates.   Thanks, CAK
